- Severity: high (multiple agents reporting failed chats)

Asha — thanks for flagging this and sending the logs. We're investigating now.

Immediate notes:
- We've seen a correlated uptick in p95/p99 on the hosted streaming frontends in the same window; on-call is looking at ingress queuing and the router cache layer.
- For an immediate mitigation, we can: 1) enable a per-tenant streaming circuit-breaker to failover to the non-streaming (polling) API, or 2) throttle internal batching to reduce long tail per-request. Option 1 will be quickest for Retailly specifically.

I'll coordinate a temporary failover while Soojin and Jonas dig into root cause. I'll loop in exec if this looks like it will persist.

Triage summary (initial):
- What I see from metrics/Grafana: a sharp increase in request queue length at the streaming ingress at ~18:18 UTC; p99 token-emit latency jumps and a rise in backend gRPC retries to the model pool.
- Hypothesis: temporary hotspot on a subset of frontends serving SSE connections; when KV cache misses + long-running responses coincide we see head-of-line blocking on the connection worker.

Immediate steps I'm taking now:
1) Requesting a targeted tenant circuit-breaker for retaily (will cause streaming requests to return 503 with a header advising fallback, so their client can switch to poll).
2) Temporarily reducing batching window from 150ms -> 50ms for frontends in us-east-1 to reduce token emission bursts.
3) Capturing expanded debug traces for any requests showing >5s token latency.

I will escalate to runtime infra if we see kernel-level stalls or GPU-side slowdowns from the model pod.

—Soojin
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Operational actions taken (19:30 UTC):
- Scaled streaming frontends in us-east-1 +2 replicas (immediate autoscale applied).
- Applied tenant circuit-breaker = true for Retailly (their streaming endpoint will now respond with header X-Stream-Fallback: true). Please advise client to switch.
- Enabled a short-term request admission cap for long-polling responses (drop >30s in favor of error path) — we're keeping a close eye on error-rate delta.

Subject: RE: Production: evening chat errors / timeouts — Exec summary and next steps

Asha —

Thank you for your patience and for sending the logs. Quick executive summary:
- Incident: evening peak p99 regressions on streaming chat (SSE) impacting Retailly from ~18:18–18:45 UTC.
- Mitigation applied: tenant-level streaming circuit-breaker activated (traffic now falling back to polling), streaming frontends scaled +2 replicas, and batching window reduced in us-east-1. Early telemetry shows p99 for Retailly returning toward baseline; we'll continue to monitor for two hours.
- Root-cause hypothesis: transient ingress hotspot + KV cache miss amplification causing head-of-line blocking on connection workers; longer-term fix will likely be a routing and cache warmup change plus finer-grained per-tenant admission control.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Soojin: collect full trace set and confirm model-pod side latencies (ETA 8 hours).
- Jonas: validate autoscale stability and roll a safe config to remove admission cap if healthy (ETA 4 hours).
- Marcus/CS: coordinate client fallback docs and a small credit for Retailly for the impact (I'm preparing a PR to finance).

We apologize for the disruption. We'll follow up with a post-incident report and a proposed mitigation roadmap. If you'd like a quick call now to walk through the temporary client-side steps (switching to poll), I'm available.

Best,
Marcus Lin
